subject: Mathematics

source.subtopic: Use and name unitary and non-unitary fractions (1/2, 1/4, 1/3, 1/5, 1/6, 1/8, 3/4, 2/5, 2/4 etc.); note that 2/4 = 1/2 and 4/4 and 3/3 = 1 whole

show.line: Cut the pizza into quarters. Eat three pieces. That is three quarters! One quarter is left.

rounds.prompt: Which picture shows three quarters coloured?
rounds.praise: Yes! Three out of four parts.

rounds.prompt: Which picture shows two fifths coloured?
rounds.praise: Yes! Two out of five parts.

rounds.prompt: Two quarters of the chocolate. That is the same as one what? Say it.
Four quarters. How much of the pizza is that?
rounds.praise: Yes! Four quarters make one whole.

rounds.prompt: Less than a half, or more than a half? Sort the pictures.
Which card names this fraction? Three parts out of three.
rounds.praise: Yes! Three thirds make one whole.

rounds.prompt: One eighth of the cake. Which piece is it?
rounds.praise: Yes! Eight equal pieces, one of them.

hints: The bottom number says how many equal parts. The top says how many you have.
All the parts together make one whole.

beat_the_tutor.setup: My turn! The bar has four parts. Two are coloured.
beat_the_tutor.tutor_try: Two quarters. That is more than a half!
beat_the_tutor.win_line: You caught me! Two quarters is exactly a half, not more.
beat_the_tutor.gentle_line: Let's look together. Two out of four is the same as one out of two. A half!

parent_line: Can name fractions like three quarters and knows two quarters is a half.
